notes: Modern Standard Arabic, phonemic/broad. Every row is harvested from English Wiktionary via the kaikki.org machine-readable export (https://kaikki.org/dictionary/Arabic/kaikki.org-dictionary-Arabic.jsonl, downloaded 2026-09-07, 77,339 entries); `sourceUrl` points at the Wiktionary page the row came from. VARIETY: only untagged pronunciations are used — those are Wiktionary's MSA transcriptions. Every row tagged or noted as a dialect (Hijazi, Egyptian, Moroccan, Levantine, Gulf, Iraqi, Tunisian, Kuwaiti, ...) was discarded rather than tagged, so the file contains no dialect forms. ʾIʿRĀB: pausal throughout, and enforced, not assumed. A row is kept only when its vocalised form carries no final short-vowel or tanwin case marker, so nouns and adjectives appear in their pausal citation form (كِتَاب kitāb, not kitābun). A final vowel that is not ʔiʕrāb does not disqualify a row: the inherent vowel of a pronominal suffix (حَالُكَ, فَضْلِكَ) and the lexical ending of the 3ms perfect, which is how Wiktionary lemmatises every Arabic verb (ذَهَبَ), are both retained. Within a multi-word row the non-final words keep their case and mood vowels, which is what pausal citation means — pause affects only the utterance-final word (as-salāmu ʿalaykum, ʾallāhu ʾakbar). Fixed liturgical and proverbial formulas that Wiktionary cites with full ʾIʿrāb throughout (bi-smi llāhi r-raḥmāni r-raḥīmi, maʿa s-salāmati, kami s-sāʿatu) were excluded to keep one convention rather than mixed in with a flag. The one retained exception is the lexical adverbial accusative -an (شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا), which is inherent to the word and universally cited that way, not a case ending; strict pause would give -ā. TEXT vs VOCALIZED: `text` is the unpointed spelling with no harakat, shadda, sukun, dagger alif or tatweel — the way a real user types it. `vocalized` is Wiktionary's pointed headword, aligned to `text` and with trailing template punctuation ('kayfa ḥāluka?') stripped. Alif wasla ٱ in a vocalised form corresponds to plain ا in `text`. VALIDATION: an entry is kept only when its MSA IPA and its transliteration agree segment-for-segment under a comparator that collapses gemination (so sun-letter assimilation al-š/aš-š lines up), de-velarises the lˤ of allāh, and ignores liaison ties, syllable dots and stress. 900 candidate entries were rejected this way, including a real Wiktionary error: كيف حالك in its feminine entry is vocalised كَيْفَ حَالُكِ but given the masculine IPA /kaj.fa ħaː.lu.ka/. 56,909 more entries had no MSA IPA at all. AMBIGUITY: unpointed Arabic is heavily ambiguous, and a row carries every reading Wiktionary attests for that spelling rather than a single one. `ipa`, `romanization`, `romanizationAcademic` and `vocalized` describe the page's dominant reading (a real lemma, then the entry carrying the most senses, then part-of-speech order); `ipaAlternatives`, `romanizationAlternatives`, `romanizationAcademicAlternatives` and `vocalizedAlternatives` hold the rest and are positionally aligned with each other, index for index. `vocalizedAlternatives` is present only where Wiktionary prints a distinct pointed form for each reading; where it prints one canonical form covering several pronunciations the field is omitted rather than have a pointed form asserted for a reading the source does not point (37 rows across the two files). 161 of 446 rows carry alternatives — 94 with two readings, 42 with three, 9 with four, 9 with five, 4 with six, 2 with eight and one with nine (قدم: qaddama, qadam, qadima, qadm, qidam, qadama, qaduma, qidm, qudum) — and they are deliberately the vocabulary a learner meets first: كتاب (kitāb / kuttāb), ذهب (ḏahab / ḏahaba / ḏahhaba), بيت (bayt / bayyata), من (min / man / mann), and the addressee-gender pairs كيف حالك, من فضلك and شكرا لك (-ka / -ki). Two readings count as distinct only when their segment sequence or stress differs, so entries differing merely in notation (ʔanā vs ʔana) are collapsed. A reading is listed only where Wiktionary publishes an IPA for it, so a few spellings whose everyday sense is a clitic form remain absent: لك, قلبي, حياتي, رأسي and ليلي have no Wiktionary lemma for 'to you', 'my heart', 'my life', 'my head' or 'my night', and a row offering only lakk / qalbiyy / ḥayātiyy / raʔsiyy would mark a correct engine wrong. LIAISON: Wiktionary marks hamzat-wasl elision with U+203F and writes the linked consonant as the onset of the following syllable (mu‿l.ʿa), which leaves a vowel-less piece. Arabic has no onsetless syllable, so that consonant is re-attached to the preceding coda and the tie becomes the word boundary the text has: mu‿l.ʿa -> mul ʿa. The segment sequence is unchanged. NOTATION divergences from Wikipedia's Help:IPA/Arabic, kept rather than converted: Wiktionary writes the tie bar on the affricate (d͡ʒ) where the help page writes dʒ, and velarises the lām of allāh (lˤ), which the help page does not list. One row carries a stress mark; Wiktionary otherwise omits stress for Arabic. Symbol inventory otherwise matches the help page (ħ ʕ x ɣ θ ð q, emphatics sˤ tˤ dˤ ðˤ, long vowels aː iː uː). ROMANIZATION: Wiktionary's Arabic transliteration is scholarly (kitāb, ḏahaba) — fully vowelled, but not the plain ASCII a learner reads. `romanization` maps it to the learner form by a fixed, documented, purely orthographic substitution (ṯ->th, ḏ->dh, š->sh, ḵ->kh, ḡ->gh, ḥ/ṣ/ḍ/ṭ/ẓ->h/s/d/t/z, ā/ī/ū->a/i/u, word-initial hamza and ayin unwritten), giving 'shukran jazilan' and 'sabah al-khayr'. No vowel is added or guessed by that mapping. `romanizationAcademic` keeps the source string verbatim so every row stays traceable. Wiktionary renders a pausal ta marbuta after long ā as -h (fatāh) and elsewhere as -a (fikra); that inconsistency is the source's and is preserved. SENTENCE TIER: 100 rows. The pausal, validated, unambiguous multi-word supply is 607 entries, so this tier is capped at 100 rather than exhausted; the rows chosen are the 31 phrasebook/phrase/interjection/proverb entries (including full clauses such as أنا لا أتكلم العربية and two proverbs) plus the highest-frequency everyday compounds, ranked by the OpenSubtitles-2018 frequency of their constituent words. Political slogans, obscure botanical and anatomical compounds and one sensitive term were hand-dropped. 14 rows are three words or longer. SOURCES: rows come from the kaikki.org export except where that export lacks a field Wiktionary shows on the page; בוקר, בית and شكرا لك were taken from the Wiktionary pages themselves, fetched 2026-09-07 at the URL in each row's `sourceUrl`. NOT INCLUDED: nothing was synthesised or inferred. Every reading is one Wiktionary publishes for that headword; only the romanisation is mechanically re-spelled, as described above.
